Options shared by zutempo's functions

Source: R/options-doc.R
zutempo_options.Rd

Temporal passes options in an object, { overflow: "reject" }; zutempo takes them as named arguments, overflow = "reject" (design 6.9). Each function's help says which it takes and its default; this page says what each one means.

Details

An option that is not a single string, or a string the option does not know, is a zutempo_type_error. A value of the right kind that fails a range check, such as an increment that does not divide its unit, is a zutempo_range_error (design 10). Either condition has a field option naming the option, as does the error for a required option left out (smallest_unit of temporal_round()). An NA option is an error, not a missing result (design 6.8).

overflow

What to do with a field out of its range, such as 31 February: "constrain" (the default) moves it to the nearest valid value, "reject" raises a zutempo_range_error.

disambiguation

What to do with a wall-clock time that a time zone skips (a gap, when clocks go forward) or repeats (a fold, when they go back):

  • "compatible" (the default): the later time in a gap, the earlier in a fold, as most other software does;

  • "earlier" and "later": the earlier or later of the two candidates;

  • "reject": a zutempo_range_error.

offset

When a string or fields give both a UTC offset and a zone, what to do if they disagree, as when a zone's rules changed after the string was written:

  • "reject" (the default for zoned_date_time()): a zutempo_range_error;

  • "use": the offset decides the exact time;

  • "ignore": the zone decides, as if no offset were given;

  • "prefer": the offset when it is one the zone allows at that wall time, otherwise the zone.

In temporal_to_string(), offset is instead whether to write the offset: "auto" or "never".

Rounding

smallest_unit is the unit to round to and largest_unit the largest unit of a result: "year", "month", "week", "day", "hour", "minute", "second", "millisecond", "microsecond" or "nanosecond", singular or plural. rounding_increment rounds to a multiple of smallest_unit, and must divide the next larger unit for the time units. rounding_mode is one of Temporal's nine modes:

ModeRounds
"ceil"towards positive infinity
"floor"towards negative infinity
"expand"away from zero
"trunc"towards zero
"halfCeil"to the nearest, ties towards positive infinity
"halfFloor"to the nearest, ties towards negative infinity
"halfExpand"to the nearest, ties away from zero
"halfTrunc"to the nearest, ties towards zero
"halfEven"to the nearest, ties to the even multiple

relative_to

Years, months and weeks have no fixed length, and neither does a day in a zone with clock changes. Arithmetic on a duration() that has them takes relative_to: a plain_date(), a plain_date_time(), a zoned_date_time(), or a string that reads as one (a string with a time zone annotation is zoned). With a zoned value, days follow the zone's clock changes; with a plain one, a day is 24 hours.

See also

temporal_round(), temporal_until(), temporal_add(), zoned_date_time() and temporal_to_string(), which take these options.

Examples

temporal_add(plain_date("2026-01-31"), "P1M")
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-02-28
try(temporal_add(plain_date("2026-01-31"), "P1M", overflow = "reject"))
#> Error : 2026-02-31 is not a valid date (element 1)

# 01:30 does not exist in Lisbon on 29 March 2026.
temporal_to_zoned_date_time(
  plain_date_time("2026-03-29T01:30"),
  "Europe/Lisbon",
  disambiguation = "earlier"
)
#> <zutempo_zoned_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-29T00:30:00+00:00[Europe/Lisbon]

temporal_round(plain_time("12:30:45.5"), "second", rounding_mode = "halfEven")
#> <zutempo_plain_time[1]>
#> [1] 12:30:46
